title: Week 29 Quiz — Globalization, Technology, and the New Immigration

questions.prompt: Week 29 · Globalization, Technology, and the New Immigration: Which term best matches this definition: The intensification of cross-border economic, cultural, political, and technological connections.
questions.explanation: globalization is defined in this week as: The intensification of cross-border economic, cultural, political, and technological connections.

questions.prompt: Week 29 · Globalization, Technology, and the New Immigration: Which term best matches this definition: The decline or relocation of manufacturing employment and capacity in a region.
questions.explanation: deindustrialization is defined in this week as: The decline or relocation of manufacturing employment and capacity in a region.

questions.prompt: Week 29 · Globalization, Technology, and the New Immigration: Which term best matches this definition: Economic activity centered on data, communication, services, and knowledge.
questions.explanation: information economy is defined in this week as: Economic activity centered on data, communication, services, and knowledge.

questions.prompt: Week 29 · Globalization, Technology, and the New Immigration: Which term best matches this definition: A treaty reducing barriers to trade among participating countries.
questions.explanation: free-trade agreement is defined in this week as: A treaty reducing barriers to trade among participating countries.

questions.prompt: Week 29 · Globalization, Technology, and the New Immigration: Which term best matches this definition: Unequal access to computers, connectivity, and digital skills.
questions.explanation: digital divide is defined in this week as: Unequal access to computers, connectivity, and digital skills.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best accounts for manufacturing employment change in the late twentieth century?
choices: Foreign trade alone explains nearly all change.
Automation, trade, logistics, finance, corporate restructuring, and policy interacted differently across regions.
Immigration caused manufacturing productivity to fall everywhere.
The information economy eliminated regional differences.
questions.explanation: The week uses a multi-causal framework and requires students to distinguish national patterns from regional effects.

questions.prompt: Why can national economic growth and severe local disruption occur at the same time?
choices: National averages can rise while losses are concentrated in particular workers, industries, or regions.
If GDP rises, every community must be better off.
Local outcomes are unrelated to national policy.
Only personal testimony can measure economic change.
questions.explanation: Aggregate gains do not determine how gains and losses are distributed.

questions.prompt: Which comparison most responsibly evaluates immigration’s effects?
choices: National population totals with no local evidence
Personal testimony corroborated with demographic, labor-market, and community evidence at a defined scale
A political slogan compared with an advertisement
questions.explanation: Strong analysis combines lived experience with aggregate evidence and identifies the unit of analysis.

questions.prompt: A chart shows rising productivity while manufacturing employment falls. What can the chart establish by itself?
choices: The two trends occurred together; additional evidence is needed to identify causal mechanisms.
Manufacturing output must also have fallen.
questions.explanation: Correlation and timing can be observed, but causal attribution requires additional mechanism-specific evidence.

questions.prompt: Which policy evaluation is strongest when addressing concentrated disruption from globalization?
choices: Judge the policy only by national GDP.
Identify beneficiary, mechanism, cost, unintended effects, and measurable outcomes.
Assume any intervention is successful if well intended.
Ignore regional differences because national totals are more objective.
questions.explanation: Policy evaluation requires explicit goals, mechanisms, distributional effects, and evidence of outcomes.

shortResponse.prompt: Using at least two specific pieces of evidence, answer: How did globalization and digital technology redistribute opportunity, risk, and political power?
shortResponse.exemplar: A full-credit response states a defensible claim, uses two accurate details, explains how each supports the claim, and acknowledges one complexity or limitation.
